WHO (World Health Origination) describes electromagnetic hypersensitivity / IEI-EMF in exactly those terms. What people report varies from person to person. Commonly mentioned patterns include headaches, fatigue, sleep disruption, difficulty concentrating, tinnitus, skin sensations, dizziness, and a general sense of overstimulation or discomfort. WHO and ANSES (French Agency for Food, Environmental and Occupational Health & Safety) both note that these reports vary widely across individuals. The patterns are usually not identical from one person to the next There is no single checklist that fits everyone. Some people mainly notice changes in sleep. Others notice focus, tension, headaches, or a feeling that certain spaces are harder to tolerate. WHO states that there are no clear diagnostic criteria and that reported symptoms differ from individual to individual. title: The Origin of Shakti Technology - Signal Sanctuary
content_excerpt: The Origin of Shakti Technology Where Performance Meets Discovery Shakti technology did not originate as a health product. It was developed to solve a very specific challenge in high-performance electronic systems . In the early 1990s, engineers and audiophiles searching for the highest levels of musical realism began to recognize that electromagnetic interference (EMI) inside audio systems was degrading signal purity. Sensitive audio circuits can be affected by electromagnetic noise generated by power supplies, transformers, digital electronics, and the surrounding environment. Through experimentation with resonant circuits, a new approach emerged. Instead of attempting to fully eliminate electromagnetic fields, carefully designed circuits could interact with the surrounding field and alter its behavior . This work eventually led to the development of Shakti technology , a passive system of resonant circuits that could stabilize electromagnetic conditions around sensitive electronics. The results were immediately noticeable in high-end audio systems, where even small improvements in signal integrity can produce audible changes. Word spread quickly among audiophiles and recording engineers.
